news.headline: Nikkei, KOSPI Scale Fresh All-Time Highs as Iran Proposal Lifts Asia Risk Sentiment
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 added 1.4% and South Korea's KOSPI surged 1.83% on April 27, both notching simultaneous record highs as Asia-Pacific markets rallied after a report that Iran submitted a proposal to the U.S. to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Hang Seng futures edged fractionally higher while mainland China's CSI 300 added 0.25%. The dual record breaks — coming despite stalled U.S.-Iran peace talks over the weekend — underscore how strongly regional equities are tracking geopolitical headline flow and AI-driven tech momentum.

news.headline: China March Industrial Profits Surge 15.8% YoY, Accelerating from Jan-Feb Pace
news.body: China's industrial profits jumped 15.8% year-on-year in March 2026, accelerating from the already strong 15.2% pace recorded in the first two months of the year, supporting modest gains in the CSI 300 (+0.25%) on April 27. The data signals resilient factory-sector earnings despite elevated global energy prices linked to Middle East disruptions. Markets are watching whether momentum holds into Q2 as oil-driven cost pressures could squeeze downstream manufacturers. The print adds to the earlier Q1 GDP beat of 5.0% year-on-year and supports the case for continued equity re-rating in Chinese industrials.

news.headline: BOJ Holds at 0.75%, Cuts Growth Forecast; June Hike Signal Watched Closely
news.body: The Bank of Japan convened its April 27-28 policy meeting widely expected to leave the benchmark rate unchanged at 0.75%, but with a hawkish tilt: the quarterly outlook report is set to cut the fiscal 2026 GDP growth forecast while sharply revising inflation higher, reflecting surging fuel costs from the Iran war energy shock. Nearly two-thirds of economists in a Reuters poll expect the policy rate to reach 1.0% by end-June, and markets are focused on Governor Ueda's post-meeting press conference for explicit signalling. A hawkish hold would reinforce upward pressure on short-end JGB yields and the yen, representing a significant headwind for export-oriented Nikkei constituents.

news.headline: Brent Jumps 2% to $107 as Iran Talks Collapse; Asia Risk Assets Hold Firm
news.body: Oil prices surged more than 2% — Brent to $107.49/bbl and WTI to $96.19 — after Trump scrapped a second round of U.S.-Iran peace negotiations over the weekend and Iran's Revolutionary Guard boarded two cargo ships near the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the energy shock, Asian equities proved resilient, with the Nikkei adding 0.53% to a fresh record and the KOSPI jumping 1% to its own all-time high on April 27. The divergence between elevated oil prices and buoyant equity sentiment reflects investor confidence that Middle East disruption remains contained for now, though energy-import-heavy markets like South Korea and Japan face growing margin pressure if crude stays elevated.

news.headline: Nikkei Closes at Record 59,716 as Tech Names Lead; BOJ Hold Expected at Apr 27-28 Meeting
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 closed at a record 59,716.18 on Friday April 25, rising 0.97% and capping a third consecutive weekly gain as AI-linked semiconductor stocks outperformed. Ibiden Co surged 12.6%, Advantest gained 5.5%, and Lasertec rose 3.8%, pulling the index higher. Japan's core inflation accelerated for the first time in five months but remained below the BOJ's 2% target, keeping markets confident the central bank will hold rates at its April 27-28 policy meeting. Markets widely expect rates on hold as policymakers weigh energy-driven inflation risks against a slowing growth outlook.

news.headline: Oil Rebounds as Iran Doubles Down on Strait of Hormuz Closure, Blocks Peace Path
news.body: WTI crude rose to $96.36/bbl early Monday after Iran's president told Pakistan's PM that ongoing U.S. actions were 'undermining trust' and complicating dialogue, while Iran's deputy parliament speaker publicly threatened that controlling the strait would impact 25% of the world's economy. Peace talks collapsed over the weekend after Iran's foreign minister left Islamabad without meeting U.S. officials following Trump's order to halt negotiations. WTI logged a +13% weekly gain last week—its biggest since early March—as the Strait of Hormuz remains functionally closed to most commercial traffic. Markets remain on edge ahead of a critical FOMC meeting April 28–29, with analysts warning oil flows could take months to normalize even if the strait reopens.

news.headline: Gold Posts ~3% Weekly Loss as Hormuz Inflation Risk Weighs on Bullion Into FOMC
news.body: Gold held near $4,710–$4,718/oz heading into Monday's open, on track for roughly a 3% weekly decline, as surging energy prices driven by the Strait of Hormuz closure intensified inflation fears and bolstered expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes. The precious metal is now approximately 10% below its January all-time high of $5,595. Rising Treasury yields near 4.5% and a firmer U.S. dollar are capping upside, while the FOMC's April 28–29 meeting—where rates are expected to hold at 3.50–3.75%—will be closely watched for any hawkish pivot signals. Structural tailwinds from central bank buying and geopolitical risk provide a partial floor, but the energy-inflation channel remains the dominant near-term headwind.

news.headline: US Natural Gas Hits Oct-2024 Low on Record Storage Build, Mild Weather Outlook
news.body: US natural gas futures dropped 3.6% to $2.52/MMBtu on April 24, the lowest since October 2024, as mild spring weather suppresses heating demand and enables outsized inventory injections. The EIA reported a 103 bcf storage build for the week ended April 17—well above both the 77 bcf year-ago figure and the 64 bcf five-year average—pushing total inventories to roughly 8% above seasonal norms. Supply has also declined about 4.1 bcfd over 18 days to an 11-week low of 108.1 bcfd as low prices prompt producers including EQT to curtail output. Gas prices are down ~19% year-on-year and fell nearly 5.8% for the week, with no material demand catalyst expected until summer cooling season begins.

news.headline: US Winter Wheat Crop Hits Multi-Year Low Rating as Southern Plains Drought Deepens
news.body: Just 30% of the U.S. winter wheat crop was rated good-to-excellent as of the week ending April 27, the lowest since 2023, with nearly 90% of Nebraska and Oklahoma now under drought and over half of Texas, Oklahoma, Colorado, and Nebraska crops rated poor-to-very-poor. Kansas—the top hard red winter wheat state—saw its good-to-excellent rating fall further to approximately 24%, with some farmers consulting insurance adjusters about potential abandonment and harvest running up to three weeks early due to drought-induced stress. USDA meteorologist Brad Rippey described conditions as among the worst seen heading into the spring growing season. Some wheat futures contracts jumped more than 3% on the week as the market priced in supply risk, though ample global supplies from Russia and South America are limiting the upside.

news.headline: Copper Slips Below $6/lb as Hormuz Energy Shock Clouds Industrial Demand Outlook
news.body: Copper futures fell back below $6/lb late in the week ended April 24, relinquishing earlier gains made when Chinese pre-holiday restocking and a record 1.33 million-ton March smelter output lifted prices above that key level. Continued disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has elevated inflation risks and growth fears, creating headwinds for industrial metals via both the rate-hike channel and potential demand weakness. Copper is up 8.85% over the past month but faces near-term pressure as peace negotiations stall and Trump has signaled the U.S. naval blockade will remain until a full deal is signed. Rio Tinto reported a 9% Q1 copper production increase from Oyu Tolgoi, adding supply-side weight.
